regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument implementing the Low Voltage Directive for electrical equipment operating between 50–1000 V AC or 75–1500 V DC; requires UKCA marking and a technical file.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The complete BESS unit is electrical equipment placed on the UK market; the 1.5 MW PCS, BMS, and all LV auxiliary circuits fall within the LV scope. UKCA marking is mandatory before the unit is supplied or put into service in Great Britain.
regulatory.designImpact: A technical file must be compiled covering design, risk assessment, test evidence, and conformity assessment. The PCS and battery system must be designed and tested to an applicable harmonised standard (BS EN IEC 62933-5-2 or BS EN IEC 62619/63056) to support the declaration of conformity.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity signed by the UK Responsible Person; technical construction file retained for 10 years; UKCA mark affixed to the unit nameplate.
regulatory.gapAction: Appoint a UK Responsible Person, open the technical file, and map each sub-system to its designated standard to structure the conformity assessment programme.

regulatory.name: Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002 (SI 2002/2665)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument governing the safety and quality of electricity supply and distribution networks; applies to any equipment connected to a public distribution network.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The BESS connects in parallel with the public distribution network behind the meter; ESQCR imposes duties on the network operator and the customer's installation to maintain safe, quality supply. ENA G99 sits under ESQCR as the engineering mechanism for compliance.
regulatory.designImpact: The PCS must meet voltage, frequency, power quality, and protection requirements set by the DNO under ESQCR; islanding detection, automatic disconnection, and reconnection delays must be implemented per G99 schedules.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: G99 application acceptance letter from the host DNO; commissioning test record countersigned by DNO witness; generation connection agreement.
regulatory.gapAction: Identify the host DNO, submit the G99 pre-application notification, and confirm protection relay settings required by that DNO's network.

regulatory.name: Requirements for Connection of Generation Equipment in Parallel with Public Distribution Networks above 16 A per Phase
regulatory.summary: Engineering Recommendation mandated by every GB DNO for behind-the-meter storage connecting in parallel with the distribution network above 16 A; enforced under ESQCR.
regulatory.applicability: UK approved code — Grid connection point well above 16 A per phase (1.5 MW); ENA G99 is the DNO-enforced Engineering Recommendation under ESQCR. Grid-forming capability and specified ride-through parameters are mandatory.
regulatory.designImpact: Inverter must support grid-forming mode, loss-of-mains (LoM) protection (ROCOF and vector shift), frequency and voltage ride-through per G99 Schedule 2, and remote trip interface. Protection settings must be pre-loaded and witnessed during commissioning.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: G99 commissioning test record signed by host DNO witness; generation connection agreement; type-test certificate for the protection relay demonstrating G99 compliance.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage the host DNO to submit the formal G99 application, agree protection settings, and schedule a DNO witness commissioning test within the two-day commissioning window.

regulatory.name: Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 (SI 1989/635)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument imposing duties on employers and the self-employed to ensure electrical systems are constructed, maintained, and operated safely.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — All electrical systems within the BESS container and at the site interface; EAWR applies during installation, commissioning, operation, and maintenance. Duty holders include the installer, site operator, and any maintenance contractor.
regulatory.designImpact: All electrical work must be carried out by competent persons; isolation and lock-off procedures must be designed in; the internal LV distribution must be designed to prevent danger from shock, arc flash, and overcurrent. BS 7671 compliance is the practical route to demonstrating EAWR compliance for fixed installations.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Electrical Installation Certificate (EIC) for the internal fixed installation signed by a competent person; site-specific arc flash risk assessment; written safe system of work for commissioning and maintenance.
regulatory.gapAction: Appoint a competent electrical engineer to design the internal distribution to BS 7671 and arrange for an EIC to be issued after installation.

regulatory.name: Requirements for Electrical Installations (IET Wiring Regulations, 18th Edition)
regulatory.summary: UK wiring regulations for fixed low-voltage electrical installations; the de facto standard for demonstrating compliance with EAWR for fixed installations.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Internal LV wiring, protection coordination, earthing, and isolation within the BESS container; demonstrates compliance with EAWR 1989. Applies to all circuits from the AC gland plate inward, including auxiliary supplies, BMS, SCADA, and fire system power feeds.
regulatory.designImpact: Design must provide shock protection (ADS), correct earthing arrangement (TN-S or TT depending on DNO supply), overcurrent and fault protection on all circuits, RCD protection on auxiliary circuits, and clearly labelled isolation points accessible within the two-day commissioning programme.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Electrical Installation Certificate (EIC) with schedule of inspections and test results, signed by a qualified person (e.g., JIB-registered engineer).
regulatory.gapAction: Incorporate BS 7671 Part 7 (special installations) requirements into the internal distribution design and commission an EIC from a qualified electrician post-installation.

regulatory.name: Electrical energy storage systems — Part 5-2: Safety requirements for grid-integrated electrical energy storage systems
regulatory.summary: UKCA harmonised standard for stationary battery energy storage safety at system level; covers fire propagation, thermal runaway containment, and grid integration safety.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Complete BESS enclosure as a grid-integrated system; demonstrates compliance with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 under the UKCA Low Voltage scheme. Covers the full system including container, racks, PCS, BMS, thermal management, and fire suppression integration.
regulatory.designImpact: System must pass fire propagation and thermal runaway containment tests; ventilation, fire detection, and suppression must be integrated and validated at system level; deflagration vent area and burst pressure must be calculated; protection coordination and isolation strategy must be documented.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Type-test report from a UKAS-accredited laboratory demonstrating system-level compliance with BS EN IEC 62933-5-2; included in the UKCA technical file.
regulatory.gapAction: Identify a UKAS-accredited test house, scope the system-level test programme, and confirm whether the chosen integrator holds an existing type-test certificate that can be leveraged.

regulatory.name: Secondary cells and batteries containing alkaline or other non-acid electrolytes — Safety requirements for secondary lithium cells and batteries for use in industrial applications
regulatory.summary: Safety standard for lithium cells and battery modules used in industrial and stationary applications; covers cell-level abuse testing and module-level safety requirements.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — LFP cell modules and battery racks within the BESS; demonstrates compliance with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 at cell and module level. Applies to each battery module supplied by the cell/module manufacturer.
regulatory.designImpact: Each cell and module must pass overcharge, overdischarge, short circuit, crush, and thermal abuse tests; BMS must implement the protection functions specified in the standard; cell supplier must provide conforming test evidence.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Cell/module supplier's BS EN IEC 62619 type-test certificate from an accredited laboratory; included in the UKCA technical file.
regulatory.gapAction: Request BS EN IEC 62619 test certificates from the cell/module supplier and verify they cover the specific cell format and chemistry used in this system.

regulatory.name: Secondary cells and batteries containing alkaline or other non-acid electrolytes — Safety requirements for secondary lithium cells and batteries for use in electrical energy storage systems
regulatory.summary: System-level safety standard for lithium battery systems used in stationary energy storage; extends BS EN IEC 62619 to the assembled battery system including BMS and enclosure.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Assembled battery system (racks + BMS + enclosure) within the BESS container; demonstrates compliance with the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 at battery-system level, complementing BS EN IEC 62933-5-2 at the grid-integration level.
regulatory.designImpact: Battery system must demonstrate safe behaviour under fault conditions including thermal runaway propagation; BMS isolation, balancing, and protection functions must be validated; enclosure ingress protection and ventilation must meet the standard's requirements.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: BS EN IEC 63056 type-test certificate from an accredited laboratory for the battery system as configured; included in the UKCA technical file.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm with the chosen integrator whether their battery system holds a current BS EN IEC 63056 certificate and obtain a copy for the technical file.

regulatory.name: Electromagnetic Compatibility Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/1091)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring electrical and electronic apparatus to not cause harmful electromagnetic interference and to have adequate immunity; UKCA marking required.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The PCS (1.5 MW power electronics), BMS, SCADA gateway, and all switching equipment within the BESS generate and are susceptible to electromagnetic disturbance; UKCA marking under the EMC regime is mandatory before placing on the GB market.
regulatory.designImpact: PCS must meet conducted and radiated emission limits and immunity requirements; EMC filter design and cable screening must be specified; EMC test programme must be planned alongside the LV safety test programme.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: EMC test report to applicable harmonised standards (e.g., BS EN IEC 61000 series) from an accredited laboratory; EMC Declaration of Conformity included in the UKCA technical file.
regulatory.gapAction: Include EMC testing in the type-test programme scope and confirm the PCS supplier holds current EMC certification for the specific inverter model.

regulatory.name: Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008 (SI 2008/1597)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument implementing the Machinery Directive for machinery placed on the GB market; applies to automated or power-driven equipment with moving parts.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The liquid cooling skid (pumps, fans, motorised valves) and any automated mechanical actuators within the BESS constitute machinery; UKCA marking under the Machinery regime is required if the cooling skid is supplied as a sub-assembly or integrated unit.
regulatory.designImpact: Cooling skid must have guarded moving parts, emergency stop provision, and a machinery technical file; risk assessment to BS EN ISO 12100 must cover all hazardous moving parts accessible during maintenance.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Machinery Declaration of Conformity and CE/UKCA mark for the cooling skid; risk assessment to BS EN ISO 12100 included in the technical file.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm whether the cooling skid supplier provides a Machinery Declaration of Conformity and obtain it; if not, commission an independent risk assessment to BS EN ISO 12100.

regulatory.name: Pressure Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/1105)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument governing the design, manufacture, and conformity assessment of pressure equipment and assemblies; applies to vessels, piping, and fittings above threshold pressures.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The liquid cooling loop (glycol/water circuit, pressurised pipework, expansion vessel, chiller refrigerant circuit) constitutes pressure equipment; PESR applies to the manufactured cooling assembly if any component exceeds the pressure/volume thresholds in Schedule 1.
regulatory.designImpact: Pressurised components must be designed to withstand maximum allowable pressure; relief valves, pressure gauges, and safe-failure modes must be specified; the cooling skid supplier must provide conformity assessment documentation.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Pressure equipment Declaration of Conformity and CE/UKCA mark from the cooling skid manufacturer; pressure test records for the assembled loop.
regulatory.gapAction: Request pressure equipment conformity documentation from the cooling skid supplier and verify that the refrigerant circuit (if present) is covered by a separate F-Gas and pressure equipment compliance declaration.

regulatory.name: Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015 (SI 2015/51)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument imposing duties on clients, designers, and contractors for health and safety in construction projects; applies to installation of the BESS on a prepared site.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Site installation of the BESS (concrete pad preparation, container placement, anchorage, AC tie-in, commissioning) constitutes construction work; CDM 2015 applies. If more than one contractor is involved or the project exceeds notification thresholds, a Principal Designer and Principal Contractor must be appointed.
regulatory.designImpact: A pre-construction health and safety file must be prepared; lifting plan for the 25–40 t container must be documented; foundation anchor design must be reviewed by a structural engineer; emergency services access routes must be established before commissioning.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: CDM health and safety file; lifting plan signed by a competent lift supervisor; structural engineer's sign-off on foundation and anchorage design; F10 notification to HSE if project is notifiable.
regulatory.gapAction: Appoint a Principal Designer at project inception and confirm whether the installation programme triggers CDM notification thresholds; commission a structural engineer for the foundation and anchorage design.

regulatory.name: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974
regulatory.summary: Primary UK health and safety legislation imposing general duties on employers, designers, manufacturers, and suppliers to ensure safety of persons at work and affected by work activities.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Applies throughout design, manufacture, transport, installation, commissioning, operation, and maintenance of the BESS; the founder as manufacturer and the site operator as employer both carry duties. Section 6 imposes duties on designers and manufacturers to ensure the product is safe and to provide adequate information.
regulatory.designImpact: Safety information, maintenance manuals, and hazard warnings must be provided with the unit; thermal runaway and fire emergency procedures must be documented; arc flash and electrical hazard assessments must be available to site personnel.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Safety data sheets for electrolyte and fire suppressant; operation and maintenance manual with emergency procedures; COSHH assessment for glycol coolant and fire suppressant agent.
regulatory.gapAction: Prepare a Section 6 HSWA information pack including safety data sheets, O&M manual, and emergency response procedures, and ensure these are handed over at commissioning.

regulatory.name: Restriction of the Use of Certain Hazardous Substances in Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2012 (SI 2012/3032)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument restricting hazardous substances (lead, mercury, cadmium, hexavalent chromium, PBBs, PBDEs, and four phthalates) in electrical and electronic equipment placed on the GB market.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The BMS electronics, PCS control boards, SCADA gateway, and auxiliary LV equipment within the BESS are electrical and electronic equipment subject to RoHS; the battery cells themselves are exempt as industrial batteries but the electronic sub-assemblies are not.
regulatory.designImpact: All PCBs, connectors, and electronic assemblies must use RoHS-compliant materials; supplier declarations of conformity must be collected for all electronic sub-assemblies.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: RoHS Declaration of Conformity from each electronic sub-assembly supplier; included in the UKCA technical file.
regulatory.gapAction: Issue RoHS compliance questionnaires to all electronic sub-assembly suppliers and collect declarations of conformity for the technical file.

regulatory.name: Batteries and Accumulators (Placing on the Market) Regulations 2008 (SI 2008/2164) as amended
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument controlling the placing on the market of batteries and accumulators; imposes labelling, registration, and take-back obligations.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The LFP battery modules and assembled battery system are industrial batteries placed on the GB market; the regulations require the crossed-out wheelie bin symbol, capacity labelling, and registration with a producer compliance scheme.
regulatory.designImpact: Battery modules must carry the crossed-out wheelie bin symbol and chemical composition marking; the founder must register as a battery producer with an approved compliance scheme before first supply.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Producer registration certificate with a UK-approved battery compliance scheme; labelling compliance evidence on battery modules.
regulatory.gapAction: Register with a UK battery producer compliance scheme (e.g., Valpak, Ecosurety) before first unit is placed on the GB market.

regulatory.name: Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013 (SI 2013/3113)
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring producers of electrical and electronic equipment to finance the collection, treatment, and recycling of waste EEE.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The BESS as a whole, and its electronic sub-assemblies (BMS, PCS control, SCADA), are EEE placed on the GB market; the founder must register as a producer and join a compliance scheme.
regulatory.designImpact: Unit must carry the crossed-out wheelie bin symbol; end-of-life take-back and recycling obligations must be documented in the O&M manual and customer contract.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: WEEE producer registration number; compliance scheme membership certificate; WEEE labelling on the unit.
regulatory.gapAction: Register with a UK WEEE compliance scheme before first supply and include end-of-life obligations in the customer contract and O&M manual.

regulatory.name: UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, Part III, Sub-section 38.3 — Lithium Metal and Lithium Ion Batteries
regulatory.summary: Mandatory transport safety tests for lithium cells and batteries; required before any shipment by road, sea, or air.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — LFP cell modules and assembled battery racks during transport from manufacturer to UK site; UN 38.3 is mandated by the Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009 (CDG 2009) for road transport and by IMDG/IATA for sea and air. ADR Class 9 dangerous goods documentation required for road legs.
regulatory.designImpact: Cells must pass altitude simulation, thermal cycling, vibration, shock, overcharge, and forced discharge tests before transport; battery modules must be packaged and labelled per ADR Class 9 requirements; the 25–40 t loaded container transport requires a dangerous goods note and driver training.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UN 38.3 test summary report from cell/module supplier or accredited laboratory; ADR dangerous goods transport document for each road movement; driver ADR certificate.
regulatory.gapAction: Obtain UN 38.3 test summary reports from the cell/module supplier and prepare ADR Class 9 transport documentation for the road delivery to site.

regulatory.name: Series 1 Freight Containers — Specification and Testing — Part 1: General Cargo Containers for General Purposes
regulatory.summary: Structural specification and test standard for ISO series 1 freight containers; the basis for the CSC plate. Certification is voided once the container shell is structurally modified.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — The 40 ft High Cube container shell as originally manufactured; the original CSC plate and ISO 1496-1 certification are voided once structural modifications are made (roof penetrations for HVAC skid, deflagration vent panels, cable gland plates, internal rack bracing). Once modified, the container must be re-certified by an alternative structural route. The unmodified container dimensions and corner casting geometry are confirmed to ISO 1496-1 and ISO 1161.
regulatory.designImpact: Original CSC plate is voided by HVAC roof penetrations and deflagration vent cut-outs; design must rely on alternative structural certification (FEA to BS EN 1993 or classification-society inspection) to demonstrate structural adequacy under transport and operational loads including the 25–40 t payload.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Finite element analysis report to BS EN 1993 or new structural certification from a recognised classification society or structural engineer; retained in the technical file.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission a structural engineer to assess the modified container under transport and operational loads and produce a structural certification report before first shipment.

regulatory.name: National Fire Chiefs Council — Grid Scale Battery Energy Storage Systems: Operational Guidance for the Fire and Rescue Service
regulatory.summary: NFCC operational guidance for fire and rescue services attending BESS incidents; sets de facto planning and design expectations for fire separation, access, detection, and suppression that planning authorities and insurers apply.
regulatory.applicability: UK approved code — Fire safety design of the complete BESS installation; while not statutory, NFCC guidance is cited by planning authorities, building control, and commercial insurers as the benchmark for acceptable fire risk management for grid-scale BESS in the UK. Non-compliance will likely prevent planning consent and insurance placement.
regulatory.designImpact: Minimum 3 m fire separation from property lines, occupied buildings, and other ESS units must be maintained; emergency services access on at least one long side; off-gas, VOC, smoke, and heat detection must be integrated; fire suppression system must be specified and maintained; thermal runaway propagation prevention must be demonstrated (UL 9540A test data accepted as evidence).
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Fire risk assessment referencing NFCC guidance; site layout drawing showing separation distances; fire suppression system commissioning certificate; UL 9540A thermal runaway propagation test report (from integrator or independent test); fire strategy document accepted by the local fire and rescue service or building control.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage a fire engineer to prepare a fire strategy document referencing NFCC guidance, confirm separation distances on the proposed site layout, and obtain UL 9540A test data from the chosen integrator.

regulatory.name: Standard for the Installation of Stationary Energy Storage Systems
regulatory.summary: US reference standard for stationary ESS installation; not UK statutory but widely cited by UK insurers and NFCC guidance as a design reference for fire safety, spacing, and suppression.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — Fire safety design and deflagration vent sizing; NFPA 855 is a US standard with no statutory force in the UK. The UK statutory peer is BS EN IEC 62933-5-2 for system safety and NFCC guidance for installation fire safety. Insurers and some planning authorities may request alignment with NFPA 855 spacing and suppression requirements.
regulatory.designImpact: Deflagration vent panels must be sized per NFPA 855 Chapter 12 calculations; suppression system density and agent selection should be cross-referenced; spacing requirements (3 m minimum) align with NFCC guidance and should be adopted in the site layout.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Not mandated; insurer may request a NFPA 855 alignment statement or gap analysis. Deflagration vent calculation pack should be retained in the technical file regardless.
regulatory.gapAction: Prepare a deflagration vent area calculation and cross-reference the site layout against NFPA 855 Chapter 12 spacing tables; include in the fire strategy document for insurer review.

regulatory.name: Test Method for Evaluating Thermal Runaway Fire Propagation in Battery Energy Storage Systems
regulatory.summary: US test method for evaluating thermal runaway propagation at cell, module, unit, and installation level; accepted by NFCC and UK insurers as evidence of fire propagation control.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — Thermal runaway propagation risk for the LFP battery system; UL 9540A is a US test method with no statutory force in the UK but is the recognised evidence base cited in NFCC guidance and required by most UK commercial insurers for grid-scale BESS. Without UL 9540A data, insurance placement will be very difficult.
regulatory.designImpact: Battery system must be tested at cell, module, unit, and installation level to demonstrate that thermal runaway does not propagate beyond a defined boundary; results directly inform fire suppression system design, rack spacing, and ventilation requirements.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UL 9540A test report for the specific battery system configuration (cell format, module design, rack arrangement) from the integrator or an accredited test laboratory; provided to insurer and included in the fire strategy document.
regulatory.gapAction: Request UL 9540A test reports from the chosen integrator for the specific LFP cell and module configuration; if not available, budget for independent testing before seeking insurance placement.

regulatory.name: Commercial Property and Liability Insurer Requirements for Grid-Scale BESS
regulatory.summary: Insurer-specific underwriting conditions for commercial BESS installations; typically require evidence of fire suppression, thermal runaway testing, separation distances, and maintenance regimes before cover is bound.
regulatory.applicability: Insurer best-practice — The complete installed BESS as a commercial asset; UK commercial property and liability insurers will impose conditions before binding cover, including evidence of NFCC guidance compliance, UL 9540A data, fire suppression commissioning, and a maintenance contract. Without insurance, the project cannot proceed commercially.
regulatory.designImpact: Fire suppression system must be maintained under a service contract; a site-specific fire risk assessment must be in place; thermal runaway propagation test data must be available; separation distances must be documented; a 24/7 remote monitoring and alarm response plan must be in place.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Insurer pre-placement questionnaire completed with supporting evidence pack (fire strategy, UL 9540A data, suppression commissioning certificate, maintenance contract, remote monitoring agreement); insurer acceptance letter before energisation.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage a specialist energy storage insurance broker (e.g., Marsh, Lockton, or a Lloyd's syndicate with BESS appetite) at design stage to obtain indicative underwriting terms and identify evidence requirements before the system is ordered.

regulatory.name: Water Supply (Water Quality) Regulations 2016
regulatory.summary: Statutory quality standards for water supplied for human consumption in England; sets parametric values for TDS, microbiological, chemical, and disinfection by-product limits.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Permeate output entering any public or private supply network; Regulation 4 requires water supplied for human consumption to meet parametric values. Applies directly where the unit supplies a UK municipal or construction-site network.
regulatory.designImpact: Post-treatment train (remineralisation, chlorination) must be sized and controlled to achieve <500 mg/L TDS, residual free chlorine 0.2–0.5 mg/L, and all Schedule 1 parametric values; PLC must log and alarm on out-of-spec permeate before it reaches the distribution point.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Water quality test reports from an accredited laboratory demonstrating compliance with Schedule 1 parametric values; operational monitoring plan accepted by the relevant water undertaker or Drinking Water Inspectorate.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage a UKAS-accredited water testing laboratory to define the commissioning water-quality test protocol and confirm which parametric values are critical for the target seawater feed chemistry.

regulatory.name: Food Safety Act 1990
regulatory.summary: Primary UK legislation making it an offence to supply water or food that is injurious to health or not of the nature, substance, or quality demanded.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Potable water output supplied to human consumers; water is a 'food' under the Act. Applies to all deployment scenarios where permeate is consumed by people.
regulatory.designImpact: Design must prevent cross-contamination between chemical dosing streams (antiscalant, sodium bisulphite, sodium hypochlorite) and the permeate circuit; interlocks must prevent out-of-spec water from reaching the outlet.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: HACCP-style hazard analysis for the water treatment process; documented interlocks and alarms in the PLC programme; operator training records.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission a HACCP analysis of the full process train and incorporate critical control points into the PLC control logic specification.

regulatory.name: Hygiene of Foodstuffs Regulation (retained UK law)
regulatory.summary: Requires food business operators to implement HACCP-based food safety management; water production for human consumption falls within scope.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Water production for human consumption; retained EU law applicable in Great Britain. Requires documented HACCP system for any operator producing water as a food.
regulatory.designImpact: Process design must identify and control critical control points (pre-treatment, RO rejection, disinfection dosing); design must allow cleaning and disinfection of all product-contact surfaces.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Written HACCP plan covering the full process train; cleaning and disinfection procedure document; records of CCP monitoring.
regulatory.gapAction: Incorporate HACCP plan development into the product documentation package; align with Food Safety Act 1990 HACCP work above.

regulatory.name: Drinking Water System Components — Health Effects
regulatory.summary: US/international standard for materials and products in contact with potable water; widely adopted as the benchmark for product-contact material safety in UK water industry procurement.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — All potable-water-contact materials (permeate pipework, post-treatment vessels, dosing wetted parts, outlet manifold); not UK statute but specified in the research report and required by most UK water utility procurement frameworks and insurers.
regulatory.designImpact: All wetted components on the permeate side (LP piping, remineralisation vessel, chlorination dosing wetted path, outlet flange) must be sourced from NSF/ANSI 61-certified suppliers; material traceability records required.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: NSF/ANSI 61 certificates of conformity from each component supplier for all potable-contact wetted parts; bill of materials cross-referenced to certificates.
regulatory.gapAction: Compile a potable-contact materials register and obtain NSF/ANSI 61 certificates from each supplier before procurement sign-off.

regulatory.name: Drinking Water System Components — Lead Content
regulatory.summary: Defines 'lead-free' wetted-surface lead content (weighted average ≤0.25%) for components in contact with potable water.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — All potable-water-contact metallic components (valves, fittings, outlet flanges on permeate side); specified in the research report and required by UK water utility procurement and US export markets.
regulatory.designImpact: All metallic wetted components on the permeate circuit must be specified and procured as NSF/ANSI 372 'lead-free'; brass fittings must be verified; substitution of any fitting requires re-verification.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: NSF/ANSI 372 certificates of conformity for all metallic potable-contact components; included in the materials register alongside NSF/ANSI 61 evidence.
regulatory.gapAction: Add NSF/ANSI 372 compliance column to the potable-contact materials register and confirm with each supplier at RFQ stage.

regulatory.name: Suitability of Non-Metallic Products for Use in Contact with Water Intended for Human Consumption
regulatory.summary: UK standard for testing non-metallic materials (plastics, elastomers, coatings) in contact with potable water; used by UK water utilities and regulators as the domestic benchmark.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Non-metallic potable-contact materials (UPVC/HDPE permeate pipework, FRP remineralisation vessel, elastomeric seals, coatings); demonstrates compliance with Water Supply (Water Quality) Regulations 2016 Regulation 4 for material safety.
regulatory.designImpact: All non-metallic wetted components on the permeate side must be sourced from suppliers holding BS 6920 approval; FRP post-treatment vessel liner and UPVC/HDPE permeate pipework must be specified accordingly.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: BS 6920 test certificates or WRAS approval certificates for each non-metallic potable-contact component; WRAS Product Approval List cross-reference acceptable.
regulatory.gapAction: Check WRAS Product Approval List for each non-metallic permeate-side component and obtain BS 6920 test certificates for any not already listed.

regulatory.name: Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument implementing low-voltage directive obligations; requires electrical equipment operating between 50–1000 V AC to be safe and UKCA-marked.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Complete electrical installation within the container (MCC/VFD panel, HP pump motor, dosing pump motors, PLC/HMI, lighting, HVAC); all electrical equipment supplied at 380–460 V 3-phase falls within scope.
regulatory.designImpact: All electrical equipment must be designed and selected to eliminate risk of electric shock, fire, and mechanical hazard; panel must be IP65-rated (NEMA 4X as specified); VFD and motor starters must carry UKCA or recognised third-party marks.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity for the assembled electrical panel and each major electrical component; technical construction file; test certificates for IP65 rating of enclosure.
regulatory.gapAction: Appoint electrical panel builder to prepare technical construction file and UKCA Declaration of Conformity for the MCC/VFD panel assembly.

regulatory.name: Electromagnetic Compatibility Regulations 2016
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring electrical and electronic apparatus to not cause harmful electromagnetic interference and to have adequate immunity.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — VFD-driven HP pump motor (45–75 kW), PLC, HMI, and dosing pump drives; VFDs are significant EMC emission sources and must comply before UKCA marking.
regulatory.designImpact: VFD must include or be fitted with an EMC filter rated for the cable run length and motor power; screened motor cables required; panel earthing strategy must address high-frequency earth currents from VFD switching.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity citing EMC Regulations 2016; EMC test report or technical construction file demonstrating compliance with BS EN IEC 61800-3 (VFD EMC standard) for the installed configuration.
regulatory.gapAction: Specify VFD with integral Class C2 EMC filter and screened motor cable; include EMC compliance in panel builder scope and obtain test evidence.

regulatory.name: Requirements for Electrical Installations (IET Wiring Regulations, 18th Edition)
regulatory.summary: UK wiring regulations governing the design, installation, and verification of fixed electrical installations; de facto enforcement standard for EAWR 1989 in fixed installations.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — All fixed low-voltage wiring within the container (power distribution, motor circuits, control wiring, lighting, socket outlets); demonstrates compliance with Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 for the fixed installation.
regulatory.designImpact: Installation must comply with shock protection (ADS), earthing and bonding (including equipotential bonding of all metallic pipework and skid frame), overcurrent protection, isolation and switching, and wiring in wet/damp locations (IP requirements for a water-processing environment).
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Electrical Installation Certificate (EIC) signed by a competent person (Part P or equivalent), with Schedule of Inspections and Schedule of Test Results; periodic inspection report at commissioning.
regulatory.gapAction: Include BS 7671 EIC in the factory acceptance test (FAT) deliverables; appoint a qualified electrician to inspect and certify the installation before first dispatch.

regulatory.name: Electricity at Work Regulations 1989
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument placing duties on employers and employees to prevent danger from electrical systems in the workplace.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — All electrical systems within the container during manufacture, commissioning, and operation; Regulation 4 requires electrical systems to be constructed and maintained to prevent danger.
regulatory.designImpact: Isolation and lockout/tagout provisions must be designed in (main isolator accessible before entering container); safe working procedures for HP pump and VFD maintenance must be documented.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Risk assessment for electrical work on the unit; isolation procedure in the operations and maintenance manual; evidence of competent-person inspection (BS 7671 EIC satisfies the installation element).
regulatory.gapAction: Include electrical isolation and LOTO procedure in the O&M manual; confirm main isolator position and labelling in the panel design.

regulatory.name: Pressure Systems Safety Regulations 2000
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument governing the safe design, installation, operation, and maintenance of pressure systems containing relevant fluids above threshold pressures.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — HP pump outlet, RO pressure vessels (55–70 bar operating, FRP vessels rated 69–83 bar), ERD, and all HP duplex stainless pipework; seawater at >0.5 bar in vessels >250 bar·litre product qualifies as a relevant fluid system.
regulatory.designImpact: A Written Scheme of Examination (WSE) must be prepared by a competent person before the system is operated; HP pressure vessels and pipework must be designed with pressure relief; operating limits must be defined and marked.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Written Scheme of Examination prepared and certified by a competent person (typically an insurance engineer or independent inspection body); pressure test records for HP pipework and vessels; CE/UKCA pressure equipment marking on vessels and fittings.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage an insurance inspection body (e.g., Lloyd's Register, Bureau Veritas, or Zurich Engineering) at design stage to scope the Written Scheme of Examination and confirm pressure vessel certification requirements.

regulatory.name: Pressure Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument implementing PED obligations for pressure equipment placed on the market; requires conformity assessment and UKCA marking for pressure equipment above threshold pressures.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — RO FRP pressure vessels (69–83 bar rated), HP pump casing, ERD pressure body, and HP duplex stainless pipework (DN>25, PS>0.5 bar); all fall within Category II–III pressure equipment scope requiring notified body involvement.
regulatory.designImpact: RO pressure vessels and HP pipework assemblies must be designed to harmonised standards (e.g., BS EN 13445 for unfired pressure vessels or ASME equivalent with UK acceptance); UKCA marking required; design dossier and conformity assessment required.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity for each pressure vessel and HP pipework assembly; notified body certificate for Category II/III equipment; material certificates (EN 10204 3.1) for HP duplex stainless pipework.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm pressure equipment category classification for RO vessels and HP pipework with a UK-approved body; obtain UKCA-marked pressure vessels from supplier or arrange conformity assessment for fabricated HP pipework.

regulatory.name: Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring machinery placed on the market to be safe and accompanied by a Declaration of Conformity and CE/UKCA marking.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The complete containerised unit constitutes an 'assembly of machinery' (HP pump, VFD, dosing pumps, automated valves, PLC control); the assembled system must be treated as a machinery assembly requiring a single UKCA Declaration of Conformity.
regulatory.designImpact: Risk assessment to BS EN ISO 12100 required for the complete assembly; guarding of rotating parts (pump couplings), emergency stop provision, and safe isolation must be designed in; technical file must be compiled.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UKCA Declaration of Conformity for the machinery assembly; technical file including risk assessment (BS EN ISO 12100), circuit diagrams, and O&M manual; CE/UKCA marks on individual machines (HP pump, dosing pumps).
regulatory.gapAction: Initiate machinery risk assessment to BS EN ISO 12100 covering the full process train; assign technical file compilation responsibility to the lead systems integrator.

regulatory.name: Safety of Machinery — General Principles for Design — Risk Assessment and Risk Reduction
regulatory.summary: Harmonised standard providing the methodology for machinery risk assessment and risk reduction; designated standard under the Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008.
regulatory.applicability: UK designated standard — Complete machinery assembly (HP pump, ERD, dosing pumps, automated valves, PLC); demonstrates compliance with Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008 essential health and safety requirements.
regulatory.designImpact: Systematic hazard identification required for all machinery interactions (rotating pump couplings, high-pressure fluid release, chemical dosing, automated valve actuation); risk reduction hierarchy must be documented and residual risks communicated in the O&M manual.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Formal risk assessment document to BS EN ISO 12100 methodology, signed off by a competent person; included in the machinery technical file.
regulatory.gapAction: Engage a machinery safety engineer to conduct the BS EN ISO 12100 risk assessment during detailed design phase, before FAT.

regulatory.name: Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument placing duties on designers, principal designers, and principal contractors for health and safety in construction projects, including installation of plant on construction sites.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Installation of the containerised unit on construction sites and potentially on remote-island or disaster-relief sites involving civil works (foundation pad, pipework connections, electrical connection); the founder as designer has duties under Regulation 9 to eliminate or reduce foreseeable construction-phase risks.
regulatory.designImpact: Design must consider safe installation sequence (container lifting points, foundation pad load specification, connection sequencing); pre-installation information pack must be provided to the principal contractor; residual risks must be communicated.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Pre-construction information pack including foundation specification, lifting plan, connection sequence, and residual risk register; Health and Safety File for handover to the client.
regulatory.gapAction: Prepare a CDM designer's risk register and pre-construction information pack as part of the product documentation suite; include foundation pad specification and lifting point certification.

regulatory.code: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974
regulatory.name: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974
regulatory.summary: Primary UK health and safety legislation placing general duties on manufacturers and suppliers to ensure products are safe and without risks to health when properly used.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Design, manufacture, supply, and installation of the complete unit; Section 6 places duties on the founder as designer and manufacturer to ensure the unit is safe and to provide adequate information for safe use.
regulatory.designImpact: Safe design must address HP fluid release hazards, chemical dosing hazards (sodium hypochlorite, antiscalant), electrical hazards, manual handling of membrane elements, and confined-space entry into the container.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Product safety file including risk assessments, safe operating procedures, COSHH assessments for chemicals used, and O&M manual; evidence of competent-person review.
regulatory.gapAction: Compile a product safety file covering all HSWA Section 6 obligations; include COSHH assessments for sodium hypochlorite and antiscalant chemicals.

regulatory.code: UKCA Marking Regulations (Product Safety and Metrology etc. (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019)
regulatory.name: UKCA Marking Obligations (Great Britain)
regulatory.summary: Post-Brexit conformity marking scheme for Great Britain; replaces CE marking for products placed on the GB market, requiring a UK Declaration of Conformity and UKCA mark.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — The complete containerised unit placed on the GB market; UKCA marking is required under the umbrella scheme covering Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regs 2016, EMC Regs 2016, Pressure Equipment (Safety) Regs 2016, and Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regs 2008.
regulatory.designImpact: A single UK Declaration of Conformity citing all applicable regulations must be prepared; UKCA mark must be affixed to the unit; technical files must be retained for 10 years.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UK Declaration of Conformity signed by the founder or authorised representative; UKCA mark affixed to the unit nameplate; technical files for each applicable regulation retained and available for OPSS inspection.
regulatory.gapAction: Appoint a product compliance manager to coordinate the UKCA technical file across all applicable regulations and prepare the consolidated UK Declaration of Conformity before first unit dispatch.

regulatory.name: Series 1 Freight Containers — Specification and Testing — Part 1: General Cargo Containers
regulatory.summary: Structural certification standard for ISO series 1 freight containers; CSC plate certification is voided once the container shell is structurally modified.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — Container shell structural integrity; the original CSC plate is voided once the shell is structurally modified (side-wall penetrations for feed/permeate/brine/power/HVAC louvres, access door modifications, internal skid anchor points through floor). Re-certification via alternative structural analysis is required for road transport and site deployment.
regulatory.designImpact: Original CSC plate voided by penetrations and skid anchor modifications; design must rely on alternative structural certification (FEA to BS EN 1993 or classification-society inspection) to confirm the modified container meets road-transport and site-loading requirements; lifting points must be re-certified.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Finite element analysis report or new structural certification from a recognised classification society or structural engineer; re-certified lifting point test certificates; road-transport abnormal load assessment if High-Cube option selected.
regulatory.gapAction: Commission structural analysis of the modified container (including all penetrations and skid anchor loads) and engage a classification society or structural engineer for re-certification before first dispatch.

regulatory.name: UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, Part III, Sub-section 38.3
regulatory.summary: Mandatory transport safety tests for lithium batteries; applicable only if the control system or UPS includes a lithium battery backup.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — UPS or battery backup within the PLC/control panel if lithium chemistry is used; Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009 (CDG Regs) + IATA DGR for air freight. If no lithium battery is present, this row is not applicable.
regulatory.designImpact: If a lithium UPS is specified for the PLC panel, cells must have valid UN 38.3 test summary; ADR dangerous goods documentation required for road transport of the unit with lithium battery installed.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: UN 38.3 test summary report from UPS/battery supplier; ADR dangerous goods note if lithium battery is present during road transport.
regulatory.gapAction: Confirm whether PLC panel UPS uses lithium chemistry; if so, obtain UN 38.3 certificate from supplier and prepare ADR documentation for transport.

regulatory.code: WHO Guidelines for Drinking-Water Quality (4th Edition)
regulatory.name: WHO Guidelines for Drinking-Water Quality
regulatory.summary: International reference framework for drinking water quality; not UK statute but used by disaster relief agencies, NGOs, and international procurement bodies as the baseline quality standard.
regulatory.applicability: Voluntary reference — Permeate quality for disaster relief and remote-island deployments outside UK jurisdiction; WHO GDWQ is the procurement benchmark for UNHCR, Red Cross, and island municipal authorities. UK statutory peer is Water Supply (Water Quality) Regulations 2016.
regulatory.designImpact: Post-treatment train must achieve WHO guideline values for TDS, nitrate, fluoride, arsenic, and microbiological parameters in addition to UK parametric values; PLC alarm thresholds should be set to WHO limits for international deployments.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: Water quality test report against WHO GDWQ parameters at commissioning; included in the product documentation for international procurement tenders.
regulatory.gapAction: Include WHO GDWQ parameter set in the commissioning water quality test protocol alongside UK Drinking Water Regulations parametric values.

regulatory.name: Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002
regulatory.summary: UK statutory instrument requiring employers to assess and control exposure to hazardous substances in the workplace.
regulatory.applicability: UK statutory — Sodium hypochlorite (chlorination dosing), antiscalant, and sodium bisulphite (dechlorination) used within the container; operators and maintenance personnel are exposed during chemical handling, dosing system maintenance, and CIP operations.
regulatory.designImpact: Chemical day tanks must be bunded or contained within the container; dosing system must have secondary containment; ventilation must prevent chlorine gas accumulation; PPE requirements and emergency eyewash provision must be designed in.
regulatory.evidenceRequired: COSHH assessment for each chemical used; safety data sheets from chemical suppliers; ventilation calculation demonstrating adequate dilution of chlorine vapour; emergency eyewash specification in the O&M manual.
regulatory.gapAction: Prepare COSHH assessments for sodium hypochlorite, antiscalant, and sodium bisulphite; incorporate bunding, ventilation, and eyewash provisions into the container layout design.
